structures.name: Evidence → Limitation → Decision
structures.description: Presents empirical proof or measurements, exposes their operational limitation or misinterpretation, and concludes with a definitive decision rule.

progression.description: States a clear empirical claim or industry metric.
Presents primary observation, data, or bench result.
Reveals what the measurement fails to account for or where it breaks down.
Interprets the underlying causal mechanism.
Concludes with the strategic or technical decision rule.

genome.thesis: A measurement without boundary conditions creates false operational confidence.
genome.reengagement: Demonstrating how relying solely on the metric causes failure.
genome.payoff: A robust decision boundary that prevents costly false positives.

examples.summary: Examines computational docking scores, shows they lack solubility and wetlab binding context, and establishes wetlab validation criteria.

anti_examples.reason: Hyping an algorithm score without subjecting it to physical test limitations.

structures.name: Double Hook Intensity Curve (4-Part Spoken Route)
structures.description: 4-part spoken structure pairing a short conversational direct trigger with a high-stakes pain question, building tension through escalating mechanism and resolving directly into P4 payoff.

progression.description: Short 6-12 word natural question obtaining the core thesis.
12-15 word question with high-stakes consequence and open loop.
18-24 words establishing a recognizable industry tension.
18-24 words showing the mechanism that worsens the failure.
18-24 words putting a real decision or asset on the line.
Exact restatement of the pain question returning maximum clarity.
Audible, direct answer to the pain question.
8-22 word memorable rule or audience transfer.

genome.thesis: A core problem escalated through mechanism requires an unambiguous operational answer.
genome.reengagement: Restating the exact pain question before delivering the breakthrough answer.
genome.payoff: Audible release of the tension built in P1-P3.

examples.summary: Direct: ¿Cuándo la biodiversidad se convierte en oportunidad? Pain: ¿Qué valor queda destruido cuando abastecimiento llega tarde? P1-P4 develops IP handoff breakdown.

anti_examples.reason: Starting trigger and reference with the same opening word, destroying development momentum.

structures.name: Belief → Contradiction → Explanation → Implication
structures.description: Takes a widespread industry convention, exposes an undeniable contradiction in practice, explains the structural reason, and establishes the operational implication.

progression.description: States what everyone in the industry assumes or repeats.
Presents a real scenario where this belief completely fails.
Explains why the assumption broke down (hidden variables).
Redefines how forward-looking practitioners must operate.

genome.thesis: Industry convention survives through inertia, not operational efficacy.
genome.reengagement: Illustrating the financial or operational cost of continuing the old belief.
genome.payoff: Clarity on what truly drives results.

examples.summary: Belief: Scientific milestones equal startup valuation. Contradiction: Science and business keep different books. Explanation: IP and supply chain risk. Implication: Align capitalization with lab milestones.

anti_examples.reason: Being contrarian just for shock value without providing the structural mechanism or empirical proof.

structures.name: Problem → Mechanism → Decision
structures.description: Rapid triage structure identifying a friction point, dissecting its technical cause, and prescribing an immediate actionable correction.

progression.description: States the visible bottleneck or operational friction.
Breaks down why the problem occurs at a system level.
Provides the exact operational change required.

genome.thesis: Symptoms cannot be treated without addressing the root mechanism.
genome.reengagement: Highlighting the recurring waste caused by ignoring the mechanism.

examples.summary: Problem: Unreproducible extract batches. Mechanism: Natural variation in plant harvesting season. Decision: Chemical fingerprinting before extraction.

anti_examples.reason: Offering platitudes instead of an explicit causal mechanism and decision rule.

structures.name: Intro Lab 3-Act Hook Spine (Promise → Development → Cliffhanger)
structures.description: High-retention video narrative spine dividing the opening into an unignorable promise, dynamic story development with source replacement, and a cliffhanger transitioning into longform.

progression.description: High-stakes premise, undeniable visual or audio artifact in first 3-5 seconds.
Rapid context building using VO, clean A-roll, and B-roll source replacement.
Unresolved tension or pivotal question carrying viewer into full body.

genome.thesis: An intro must establish the necessity of the entire video in under 45 seconds.
genome.reengagement: Pattern interrupt before the halfway mark of Act II.
genome.payoff: Irresistible open loop propelling viewer into the master episode.

examples.summary: Act I reveals a 40M token anomaly, Act II traces memory leakage to unindexed context, Act III asks how the team prevented catastrophic degradation.

anti_examples.reason: Giving away the complete resolution during the hook, destroying retention for the master episode.

structures.name: Framework: Problem → Mental Model → Component Parts → Governing Rules
structures.description: Constructs a reusable conceptual framework to solve recurring complex decisions, naming its component parts and defining interaction rules.

progression.description: Identifies the domain where people repeatedly make inconsistent decisions.
Introduces the overarching conceptual architecture.
Defines each pillar, layer, or module in the system.
The operational rules governing how parts interact.
How to use the framework to make immediate trade-offs.

genome.thesis: Without a shared mental model, teams optimize subcomponents at the expense of system integrity.
genome.reengagement: Contrasting ad-hoc decision making with framework-driven clarity.
genome.payoff: A permanent cognitive asset for the viewer.

examples.summary: Breakdown of MokaDex engine: Raw data ingestion → Context graph linking → Wetlab scoring → Explainable recommendation output.

anti_examples.reason: Inventing jargon acronyms that confuse rather than simplify physical realities.

structures.name: Conversation: Disagreement → Exploration → Friction Test → Synthesis
structures.description: Multi-speaker dialogue structure where two experts clash on a technical assertion, explore edge cases through joint debate, and emerge with a synthesized higher-order rule.

progression.description: Direct disagreement between two distinct perspectives.
Speaker A defends thesis with evidence; Speaker B counters with failure cases.
Stress-testing both positions against an extreme operational scenario.
Discovering the underlying boundary condition where both are reconciled.

genome.thesis: Nuance is uncovered when two experienced practitioners collide with mutual respect.
genome.reengagement: The moment where both speakers realize a third unstated variable was missing.
genome.payoff: A breakthrough synthesis superior to either initial position.

examples.summary: Debate on whether MLX Whisper on Apple Silicon is ready for live captioning vs batch queueing, arriving at optimal memory buffer bounds.

anti_examples.reason: Staging artificial conflict without technical substance or meaningful synthesis.

structures.name: Five Levels of Molecular Evidence
structures.description: Specific biotechnology evidence progression moving from computational in-silico prediction through in-vitro binding, in-vivo efficacy, safety toxicology, to human clinical validation.

progression.description: Computational docking, AI prediction, molecular dynamics.
Enzyme inhibition, cell assay, chemical fingerprinting.
Model organism efficacy, bioavailability, pharmacokinetics.
Cytotoxicity, Ames test, regulatory compliance limits.
Double-blind randomized human trial with verified endpoint.

genome.thesis: Not all scientific evidence has the same commercial or clinical weight.
genome.reengagement: Showing that 90% of in-silico hits fail Level 2 and Level 3.
genome.payoff: A rigorous auditing rubric for biotech investors and researchers.

examples.summary: Breakdown of the 5 evidence tiers for cosmetic and nutraceutical bioactives, warning against making commercial claims based purely on docking.

anti_examples.reason: Claiming a bioactive is 'clinically proven' when only Level 1 molecular docking has been performed.

structures.name: Enterprise Strategic Prequalification & Maturity Audit
structures.description: Enterprise audit structure diagnosing organizational maturity, regulatory compliance readiness, and infrastructure transition readiness before recommending deployment.

progression.description: Current infrastructure footprint and regulatory compliance status.
Uncovering single points of failure and compliance exposure.
Calculating operational expenditure vs modernization capital.
3-phase mitigation plan prioritizing critical uptime.

genome.thesis: Large-scale infrastructure modernization fails when organizations bypass baseline prequalification.
genome.reengagement: Exposing regulatory fines or operational risks of un-audited infrastructure.

examples.summary: Prequalification framework evaluating commercial energy storage feasibility based on interconnection queue delay risk.

anti_examples.reason: Pitching infrastructure solutions without analyzing regulatory compliance or grid capacity limits.

structures.name: Moka Bio 12-Topic Room Recording Ficha (Client-Specific)
structures.description: Specialized content recording ficha organized into 12 dedicated topic rooms across Science (Facu) and Commercial/IP Strategy (Rafa), balancing technical authority with investor messaging.

progression.description: Matches piece to one of 12 predefined thematic rooms.
Assigns speaker mode (Facu = wetlab rigor; Rafa = commercial strategy).
Direct trigger (6-12 words) + Pain question (12-15 words).
P1-P4 spoken references recorded live.
Definitive 8-22 word closing rule.

genome.thesis: Personal brand authority requires strict separation of scientific proof from business capitalization.
genome.reengagement: Restating the niche pain question before technical resolution.

examples.summary: Topic Room 04 (MokaDex Search): Facu explains why text keyword search in chemical papers misses 80% of active isomers.

anti_examples.reason: Turning the wetlab scientist into an aggressive sales promoter or the commercial founder into an unverified lab tech.
